format.description: Format names the format and its major version: pidl-samples/v1.

protocol.description:
Protocol is the ID of the protocol the set is for. When set, the
set applies only to that protocol.

name.description:
Name names the implementation, such as "example-sdk-go". It is the
source cited by examples the set creates for steps without one.

samples.description: Samples are the set's samples, each attached to a step.

SampleSet.description: SampleSet holds code samples for a protocol, kept apart from the protocol document.

step.description:
Step is the address of a step as written: "<scenario>/<step-id>" for
a step of a scenario or fragment, "<scenario>" for the scenario's
own samples, or "<step-id>" in a document without scenarios.

language.description:
Language names the code's language with a common highlighter name,
such as "go", "typescript", "python" or "csharp". Samples are also
representations a step's narration can be overridden for.

label.description:
Label distinguishes samples in one language, such as "Agent" and
"Resource".

role.description: Role is the entity ID whose developer writes this code.

code.description:
Code is inline code, or a source's code once resolved. A sample has
Code, Source, or both.

source.description: Source refers to a marked region of a file in a repository.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the hex SHA-256 of Code, recorded when Source is resolved.

SampleSetEntry.description: SampleSetEntry is one sample and the step it belongs to.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository's module-style path, such as
"github.com/aauth-dev/aauth-go".

ref.description:
Ref is a tag or commit to read the file at. Empty reads the
checkout's working tree.

path.description: Path is the file's path within the repository.

region.description: Region is the marked region's name.

SampleSource.description: SampleSource refers to the code between "pidl:begin <region>" and "pidl:end <region>" markers, in comments, in a file of a repository.

title: PIDL Sample Set
description: Code samples an implementation keeps apart from a protocol document, each attached to a step by its address, read by `pidl samples` and `pidl generate --samples`.
